jobs.title: Director, Data Governance
jobs.description:
McKesson is an impact-driven, Fortune 10 company that touches virtually every aspect of healthcare. We are known for delivering insights, products, and services that make quality care more accessible and affordable. Here, we focus on the health, happiness, and well-being of you and those we serve – we care.

What you do at McKesson matters. We foster a culture where you can grow, make an impact, and are empowered to bring new ideas. Together, we thrive as we shape the future of health for patients, our communities, and our people. If you want to be part of tomorrow’s health today, we want to hear from you.

About The Role

McKesson is seeking a strategic and experienced Director, Data Governance to lead enterprise-wide data governance programs that improve data quality, regulatory compliance, business trust, and operational excellence. This leader will define and execute governance strategies across data governance, metadata management, data cataloging, data quality, master data management, and data lineage capabilities.

The Director will partner with business, technology, risk, compliance, and data leaders to establish governance frameworks, standards, policies, and controls that support data-driven decision making and regulatory requirements. This role requires a strong combination of leadership, stakeholder engagement, data management expertise, and the ability to influence outcomes across a complex enterprise environment.

What You'll Do

Lead enterprise data governance strategy, operating model, policies, standards, and controls.
Drive adoption and optimization of data governance and data catalog platforms.
Establish and oversee data quality, metadata management, master data, and data lineage programs.
Partner with Risk, Compliance, Privacy, Security, and Audit teams to ensure regulatory compliance and governance readiness.
Develop governance metrics, data health KPIs, and executive reporting for senior leadership.
Engage business stakeholders to define data ownership, stewardship, accountability, and governance priorities.
Lead cross-functional teams delivering large-scale governance and data management initiatives.
Build and develop high-performing teams while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Basic Requirements

12+ years of professional experience in data governance, data management, data architecture, analytics, compliance, or related disciplines, including 4+ years of people leadership experience.
Bachelor's degree or equivalent professional experience.
Experience leading enterprise-scale data governance programs and operating models.
Experience implementing or managing data catalog, metadata management, or governance platforms.
Experience with data quality management, data lineage, data stewardship, and governance controls.
Experience partnering with compliance, risk, privacy, audit, or regulatory organizations.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional initiatives and influence senior stakeholders.
Experience defining governance policies, standards, KPIs, and reporting frameworks.

Preferred Skills/Experience

Master's degree in Information Management, Computer Science, Business, Data Analytics, or a related field.
Experience supporting regulated industries such as healthcare, pharmaceutical, financial services, or insurance.
Knowledge of data governance platforms such as Collibra, Alation, Informatica, Microsoft Purview, or similar tools.
Experience with DAMA-DMBOK principles and enterprise data management frameworks.
Knowledge of data privacy regulations, governance controls, and risk management frameworks.
Experience leading enterprise-wide data transformation initiatives.
Strong executive communication and organizational change management capabilities.
Relevant certifications related to data governance, data management, privacy, or cloud technologies.

Travel, Work Environment & Physical Requirements

Ability to travel up to 20% as business needs require.
Hybrid or remote work arrangements may be available based on business and geographic requirements.
Ability to participate in virtual and in-person meetings and work effectively in a technology-enabled environment.

For McKesson Canada:
Employees are required to be in the office two (2) days per week
, either in Ville Saint-Laurent, Quebec or Mississauga, Ontario.

We are proud to offer a competitive compensation package at McKesson as part of our Total Rewards. This is determined by several factors, including performance, experience and skills, equity, regular job market evaluations, and geographical markets. In addition to base pay, other compensation, such as an annual bonus or long-term incentive opportunities may be offered. For more information regarding benefits at McKesson, please click here.

McKesson has become aware of online recruiting-related scams in which individuals who are not affiliated with or authorized by McKesson are using McKesson’s (or affiliated entities, like CoverMyMeds or RxCrossroads) name in fraudulent emails, job postings or social media messages. In light of these scams, please bear the following in mind:

McKesson Talent Advisors will never solicit money or credit card information in connection with a McKesson job application.

McKesson Talent Advisors do not communicate with candidates via online chatrooms or using email accounts such as Gmail or Hotmail. Note that McKesson does rely on a virtual assistant (Gia) for certain recruiting-related communications with candidates.

McKesson job postings are posted on our career site: careers.mckesson.com.

McKesson is an Equal Opportunity Employer

McKesson provides equal employment opportunities to applicants and employees, without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, protected veteran status, disability, age, genetic information, or any other legally protected category. For additional information on McKesson’s full Equal Employment Opportunity policies, visit our Equal Employment Opportunity page.

McKesson is committed to being an Equal Employment Opportunity Employer and offers opportunities to all job seekers including job seekers with disabilities. If you need a reasonable accommodation to assist with your job search or application for employment, please contact us by sending an email to (United States) Disability_Accommodation@McKesson.com or (Canada) Accessibility@mckesson.ca. Resumes or CVs submitted to this email box will not be accepted.

Join us at McKesson!

jobs.title: Director of Finance And Accounting
jobs.description:
Our Client

Our client is a leading law firm in downtown Toronto
seeking a Director of Finance & Accounting
to join its Finance team. Reporting to senior Finance leadership and working closely with executive stakeholders, the successful candidate will lead an established team while identifying opportunities to strengthen processes, controls, reporting and overall revenue performance. This is an excellent opportunity for a hands-on, solutions-oriented finance leader
who enjoys both strategic oversight and getting into the details.

The role is four days per week in office in downtown Toronto
and offers a competitive compensation package.

Responsibilities
Provide end-to-end leadership of the revenue lifecycle, including WIP, billing, e-billing, rates administration, accounts receivable, collections, cash application and revenue reporting
.
Lead annual revenue planning, budgeting and forecasting and provide financial insights to support strategic and operational decision-making.
Develop and monitor key revenue and working-capital metrics, identifying trends, risks and opportunities to improve financial performance.
Drive strategies to improve realization, accelerate billing and collections, reduce aged WIP and receivables, and enhance cash flow.
Oversee billing arrangements, rate administration, alternative fee arrangements and e-billing processes.
Develop management reporting, dashboards and business intelligence solutions that provide meaningful and actionable insights.
Lead process-improvement, automation and finance-transformation initiatives
, including system implementations, upgrades and optimization projects.
Partner with Technology, Finance and other internal stakeholders to improve data quality, reporting efficiency and system utilization.
Lead, mentor and develop the revenue operations team, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration and continuous improvement.
Present financial information and recommendations to senior leadership and other key stakeholders in a clear and commercially focused manner.

Requirements
CPA designation required.

10+ years of progressive finance experience
, including meaningful leadership responsibilities.
Strong experience in revenue operations, FP&A, billing, rates, accounts receivable and/or collections
.
Demonstrated experience leading teams and driving process improvement, systems implementation and organizational change
.
Experience within a professional services environment
strongly preferred; law firm, accounting or consulting experience would be particularly relevant.
Strong financial planning, reporting, analytical and business acumen.
Advanced proficiency with Excel, financial modelling, dashboards and business intelligence tools
; Power BI experience is an asset.
Experience with ERP or practice-management systems and system implementations/upgrades; Aderant experience is an asset
.
A hands-on, solutions-oriented leadership style with the ability to balance strategic thinking with attention to detail.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the presence and credibility to work directly with senior stakeholders.
Ability to simplify complex financial information and communicate effectively with non-financial audiences.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Toronto or Waterloo, hybrid | Full-time | Reports to the CEO

Build the finance function at a fast-growing senior care technology company shipping hardware to 24 countries.

The Company

We went from a lab in Waterloo to 24 countries in five years. Our sensors detect falls and track sleep, health and wellness, with no cameras, wearables or pendants. Families get peace of mind. Older adults keep their independence. Our CTO, Dr. Yihong Qi, holds 680 patents, and the next few hundred get built here.

Why now

We are scaling. One of the largest deals in our history is in delivery, our consumer product launches in January, and we are preparing our next raise. Every one of those runs on numbers leadership can trust: a close that lands on time, a forecast that ties sales to inventory and cash, and books that hold up in diligence. This is the moment to bring in the leader who owns it.

The role

This is the senior finance role at Pontosense. You own the close, the forecast, controls and the numbers behind our next raise, across our entities in Canada and China. You work directly with the CEO and the leadership team, and you are in the room with investors. This is a builder role first and an operator role second. You set up how finance runs here, then you run it.

What You'll Own

A monthly close that is reliable and consolidated across Canada and China, landing by business day 10
A forecast the company actually runs on, with sales, inventory and cash tied together
Product costing that is right: landed cost, COGS and inventory planning for hardware built overseas
The raise: the model, the data room and investor reporting, with you in the room
Annual financials prepared and audited on time, and the relationships with our auditors and tax advisors
Controls that hold up across two countries: approvals, spend and intercompany
A seat at the leadership table

What Year One Looks Like

The books close on time every month, consolidated. The forecast is trusted, and inventory is planned, not guessed. Audited financials are current, and our next raise runs on numbers that hold up in diligence.

How We Work

Build it right, then make it better. People's safety rides on what we ship, so we test hard and never settle for good enough.
Say it as it is. Kind and direct, at every level, including the CEO.
Real impact. There is more room to make a difference here than at a company ten times our size.
Do what you said. Trust is built on follow-through, and we return it with real ownership.
Hard, and worth it. What we build keeps someone's parent safe at home. Rest well, it's part of the job.

This is for you if

You'd rather own a problem than be assigned a task
You want the mission to matter and the pace to be real
You're happy to be the person who just fixes it

This isn't for you if

You want a playbook handed to you
You need a big team before you can move

You'll thrive here if

You are a CPA who started in audit, then grew with a product or technology company, with promotions along the way
You have owned the close and built the model yourself, not just reviewed them
You have run FP&A, not only the close: budgets, forecasts and the model leadership makes decisions on
You have worked with inventory, COGS and supply chain costing. Multi-entity or international consolidation is a strong plus
You have worked with investors, a board or lenders, or are ready to step into that
You explain the numbers plainly to people outside finance, and decide with incomplete information
You are as happy reconciling an account yourself as setting the strategy

You don't need to check every box. If this sounds like you, we'd like to hear from you.

Where this goes

As we raise and scale, this role grows into leading a finance team of your own.

What You Get

A sensor for your parents, on us
Direct access to the leadership team. No layers.
Fair pay, with the opportunity for equity
Impact decides your pay and your path, not tenure
Hybrid in Toronto or Waterloo, remote if that's where you do your best work
Health, dental and vision benefits

The details

Pay: $160,000 to $190,000 CAD base salary
This is a new role, created to grow the team, not a backfill
How we hire: typically an initial interview, a short case, and a final interview in person with our CEO and members of the team. We may adjust this depending on the role
We leverage AI tools in our hiring process, but prioritize human input and manual review

Our Commitment

At Pontosense, we are committed to creating a workplace that is inclusive and accessible to all. We value diversity and believe that everyone deserves an equal opportunity to succeed.

If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation during the hiring process, please let us know. We will work with you to make the necessary accommodations to ensure a fair and positive experience for all applicants.

We strive to provide accessible communication and technology for our employees and customers and always look for ways to improve. If you have any feedback or suggestions on how we can improve accessibility in our workplace, please don't hesitate to contact us.

We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and welcome candidates from all backgrounds to apply for open positions at our company.
